children.text: Mr. Chanek just won the national chess tournament and got a huge chessboard of size $$$N \times M$$$. Bored with playing conventional chess, Mr. Chanek now defines a function $$$F(X, Y)$$$, which denotes the minimum number of moves to move a knight from square $$$(1, 1)$$$ to square $$$(X, Y)$$$. It turns out finding $$$F(X, Y)$$$ is too simple, so Mr. Chanek defines:
Given X and Y, you are tasked to find $$$G(X, Y)$$$.

A knight can move from square $$$(a, b)$$$ to square $$$(a', b')$$$ if and only if $$$|a - a'| \gt 0$$$, $$$|b - b'| \gt 0$$$, and $$$|a - a'| + |b - b'| = 3$$$. Of course, the knight cannot leave the chessboard.
The first line contains an integer $$$T$$$ $$$(1 \le T \le 100)$$$, the number of test cases.
Each test case contains a line with four integers $$$X$$$ $$$Y$$$ $$$N$$$ $$$M$$$ $$$(3 \leq X \leq N \leq 10^9, 3 \leq Y \leq M \leq 10^9)$$$.
For each test case, print a line with the value of $$$G(X, Y)$$$ modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
